subject: History
topic: Shah Jahan and his reign — mixed tiers
description: Reign 1628-1658, Mumtaz Mahal, Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Peacock Throne, Aurangzeb's coup

questions.stem: Shah Jahan ascended the Mughal throne in:

options.option_text: 1605, succeeding his father Akbar of the Mughals
1628, after the death of his father Jahangir
1658, succeeding his elder brother Dara Shukoh
1707, after the death of his son Aurangzeb

questions.explanation: Shah Jahan — born 1592 as Khurram, third son of Jahangir. Crowned in Agra on 14 February 1628 after his father Jahangir died (Oct 1627) and a brief succession struggle. Reigned 1628-1658. Distractor 1 = Jahangir's accession (after Akbar). Distractor 3 = Aurangzeb's accession after defeating Dara Shukoh in war. Distractor 4 = post-Aurangzeb period (Bahadur Shah I).

questions.stem: The TAJ MAHAL was commissioned by Shah Jahan in memory of:

options.option_text: Nur Jahan, the famous wife of his father Jahangir
Mumtaz Mahal, his wife who died in childbirth in 1631
Jahanara, his eldest daughter, devoted companion late
Hamida Banu, his great-grandmother in the Mughal line

questions.explanation: Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum) — Shah Jahan's chief consort. Died on 17 June 1631 in Burhanpur giving birth to her 14th child. Construction of the Taj at Agra started 1632, finished c. 1648-53. Chief architect — Ustad Ahmad Lahauri. UNESCO 1983. Distractor 1 = Jahangir's wife. Distractor 3 = his daughter who survived him; supported him during his last years in captivity. Distractor 4 = Akbar's mother (Humayun's wife).

questions.stem: Shah Jahan moved the Mughal capital from Agra to a newly built city. That new capital was called:

options.option_text: Fatehpur Sikri, also called the abandoned capital
Shahjahanabad, today the Old Delhi area
Akbarabad, named in honour of his grandfather
Lahore, the imperial capital of the Punjab area

questions.explanation: Shahjahanabad — new walled capital city built between 1639 and 1648 around the Red Fort (Lal Qila); centred on Chandni Chowk. Today this area is OLD DELHI. Capital shifted from Agra to Shahjahanabad in 1648. Distractor 1 — Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's capital (abandoned ~1585). Distractor 3 — Akbarabad was an alternative name for Agra under the Mughals. Distractor 4 — Lahore was an important provincial capital but not founded by Shah Jahan.

questions.stem: The famous PEACOCK THRONE (Takht-i-Taus), commissioned by Shah Jahan and adorned with the Koh-i-Noor among other gems, was eventually:

options.option_text: Destroyed by fire during a sack of Delhi in 1739
Carried away as plunder by Nadir Shah of Persia in 1739
Sent to England by Aurangzeb as a gift to King Charles
Buried at Akbar's tomb at Sikandra during the 1857 revolt

questions.explanation: Peacock Throne — built 1635, took ~7 years; chief jeweller Bebadal Khan. Adorned with Koh-i-Noor, Timur Ruby, Akbar Shah Diamond. Nadir Shah of Persia sacked Delhi (Mar 1739) defeating Muhammad Shah Rangila and carried off the Peacock Throne to Iran. The original throne was later destroyed / disassembled in Persia after his assassination (1747); the Koh-i-Noor passed through Persians, Afghans, Sikhs (Ranjit Singh), and finally to the British (1849, after annexation of Punjab). Distractor 1 — destroyed in transit, not by fire. Distractor 3 — invented. Distractor 4 — invented.

questions.stem: Shah Jahan's reign is often called the GOLDEN AGE of MUGHAL ARCHITECTURE because of works including the:

options.option_text: Qutub Minar, Iron Pillar, and Tomb of Iltutmish
Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid (Delhi), Moti Masjid
Buland Darwaza, Diwan-i-Khas, and Salim Chishti's tomb
Charminar, Golconda Fort, and Mecca Masjid (Hyderabad)

questions.explanation: Shah Jahani buildings: TAJ MAHAL (Agra, 1632-53), RED FORT / Lal Qila (Delhi, 1639-48), JAMA MASJID Delhi (1644-56, largest mosque in India then), MOTI MASJID inside Agra Fort (white marble, 1647-54), Diwan-i-Khas (Red Fort) inscribed with 'If there is paradise on earth, it is this, it is this'. Distractor 1 = pre-Mughal (Mamluk Slave dynasty). Distractor 3 = Akbar's Fatehpur Sikri buildings. Distractor 4 = Qutb Shahi (Hyderabad), a different sultanate.

questions.stem: The succession war (1657-58) at the end of Shah Jahan's reign was won by:

options.option_text: Dara Shukoh, the eldest son and Shah Jahan's chosen heir
Aurangzeb, the third son who defeated his three brothers
Shuja, the second son and governor of Bengal
Murad Bakhsh, the fourth son and governor of Gujarat

questions.explanation: Shah Jahan fell ill in 1657 → triggered succession war among his four sons: DARA SHUKOH (eldest, liberal scholar, Shah Jahan's choice, translator of Upanishads as Sirr-i-Akbar); SHUJA (Bengal); AURANGZEB (Deccan, orthodox); MURAD (Gujarat). Aurangzeb allied tactically with Murad to defeat Dara at Battle of Samugarh (1658), then betrayed Murad. Imprisoned Shah Jahan in Agra Fort (he died there 1666, watching the Taj from his window). Aurangzeb crowned 1658, ruled 1658-1707. Distractor 1 — Dara was beheaded by Aurangzeb in 1659.

questions.stem: Shah Jahan spent his last years (1658-1666) confined inside which fort by Aurangzeb?

options.option_text: Red Fort at Delhi, his own newly built capital seat
Agra Fort, with a view of the Taj Mahal across the Yamuna
Lahore Fort, in the western reaches of the empire
Gwalior Fort, traditional Mughal high-security prison

questions.explanation: Aurangzeb imprisoned his father in the AGRA FORT, not Delhi's Red Fort, in 1658. He spent 8 years there until his death in January 1666. The fort sits on the right bank of the Yamuna, with Taj Mahal a couple of km downstream. The famous Musamman Burj — the small octagonal tower in Agra Fort with a marble lattice screen overlooking the Yamuna — is where Shah Jahan is said to have spent his final hours gazing at the Taj. Tended by his daughter Jahanara, who voluntarily shared his confinement. Buried beside Mumtaz Mahal in the Taj.
